technical_and_design_decisions: Migrate each XD module into the existing s-c-s repository using the repository's established module layout, build conventions, dependency management, and packaging approach.

Preserve the externally visible module names, configuration properties, message payload behavior, and source or sink semantics unless incompatibilities with the s-c-s APIs require an equivalent adaptation.
Implement the mail source and mail sink as separate module capabilities while sharing common mail connection, authentication, and configuration code where practical.
Use the existing Spring messaging and integration abstractions in s-c-s rather than introducing a new programming model.
Target the repository's supported Java and Spring versions, assumed to be Java 17 or newer and compatible with Spring Framework 6-era APIs.
Add or migrate focused unit and module-level integration tests for configuration, message conversion, connectivity, and error handling.
Treat the migrated modules as independently buildable and publishable artifacts consistent with the other s-c-s modules.
assumptions: The source code, tests, documentation, and build metadata for all eight requested XD modules are available and can be inspected without reconstructing functionality from binaries.
The s-c-s repository already exists and provides build, test, dependency, packaging, and CI conventions that can be followed.
The migration is a repository and API adaptation rather than a redesign of module behavior or addition of new major features.
The duplicated mail user stories represent two capabilities of the mail module: mail as a source and mail as a sink.

Existing external services or local test substitutes are available for reasonable validation of TCP, mail, GPFDist, HDFS, and MongoDB integrations; provisioning production infrastructure is out of scope.

The estimate includes implementation, automated tests, documentation updates, and CI validation, but excludes release management, production deployment, operational support, and long-term maintenance.
One developer performs the complete effort, including code changes, testing, documentation, and review-fix work.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the XD implementations, module descriptors, configuration properties, existing tests, dependencies, licensing, and the target s-c-s repository conventions; identify API and packaging differences.
Create or adapt the common module structure, build descriptors, dependency declarations, configuration metadata conventions, packaging, and shared test utilities required by the migrated modules.
Port the syslog source implementation and configuration, adapt it to s-c-s APIs, preserve message and error behavior, and add or migrate focused automated tests.
Port the mail-receiving source capability, including polling or listener behavior, mail connectivity configuration, message conversion, error handling, and automated tests.
Port the TCP server/source capability, including connection handling, framing or decoding configuration, message emission, lifecycle behavior, and automated tests.
Port the TCP client/source capability, including outbound connection management, reconnection behavior, decoding, configuration, lifecycle handling, and automated tests.
Port the GPFDist sink capability, including request or stream handling, payload serialization, connection configuration, failure behavior, and automated tests.
Port the HDFS dataset sink, including filesystem configuration, dataset or file writing behavior, batching and serialization, error handling, and automated tests.
Port the mail-sending sink capability, reuse compatible shared mail configuration code, adapt message-to-email conversion and delivery behavior, and add or migrate automated tests.
Port the MongoDB sink, including client and collection configuration, payload mapping, write behavior, error handling, dependency compatibility, and automated tests.

Build all modules together, execute cross-module and integration validation, verify configuration metadata and artifact contents, test representative streaming pipeline usage, and resolve compatibility defects.
Update module documentation, configuration/property references, usage examples, migration notes, supported dependency information, and repository-level indexes or catalogs.
Add or update CI build definitions, test execution, static checks, artifact validation, and any required module-specific test profiles or service containers.
Perform a complete code and requirements review, address review findings, clean up dependency or configuration issues, and conduct final regression verification.
